requirements.requirement: node1 serves working HTTPS requests on TCP port 8443.
requirements.summary: Direct checks received HTTP 200 over TLS, confirmed the listener on 0.0.0.0:8443, and showed that the served certificate matched the certificate on disk. The service remained healthy after reboot.

requirements.requirement: The certificate is checked and renewed automatically before expiration.
requirements.summary: An enabled, active hourly persistent timer invokes the production renewal service. A certificate inside the seven-day renewal window was replaced successfully with a 30-day certificate, and the final timer and certificate state remained healthy.

requirements.requirement: The HTTPS service picks up renewed certificates while continuing to answer requests.
requirements.summary: During rotation, the served serial and fingerprint changed without a service PID change. A concurrent request stream completed 160 of 160 requests successfully with no failures. A second renewal-window test also loaded the replacement certificate without restarting the process.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. HTTPS works on port 8443, renewal-window behavior and hourly automation are configured and exercised, and certificate changes occur without request interruption. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged reboot, changed boot identity, and recovered HTTPS, certificate, timer, firewall, and listener state are directly shown and corroborated by lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: The expiring-certificate renewal was triggered by manually starting the same service used by the timer; evidence does not capture an hourly timer firing while an expiring certificate was installed. Timer activation, scheduling, persistence, and the complete renewal path are nevertheless directly demonstrated.

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unrelated state-changing experiments were identified. Certificate rotations and the reboot were bounded verification actions directly supporting the task or mandatory restart protocol. The only hygiene issue is that the necessary continuity test created /tmp/https8443-rotation-test.log and .done and did not remove them; both remained after reboot. No failed services or package damage were observed.
